channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Brasil terá 158,7 milhões de eleitores aptos a votar em 2026
item.description: Brazil will have 158.7 million eligible voters for the 2026 elections, a 1.5% increase from 2022. Growth was strongest in the North region (4.4%) and among overseas voters (31.8%), with notable increases in Roraima (9.6%), Tocantins (8.1%) and Mato Grosso (6.8%). Voters will elect the president, governor, senator, federal deputy and state/district deputy.

item.title: Craque Neto detona Ronaldo após cena com Trump: "Não precisava"
item.description: Craque Neto criticized Ronaldo Fenômeno for allowing Donald Trump to touch the 2026 World Cup trophy, calling him a 'sycophant' and saying the gesture was unnecessary and idiotic. He also accused Ronaldo of avoiding confrontation with powerful football figures like Gianni Infantino and the CBF, despite his interest in leading the organization, and of failing to speak out on the crisis facing the Brazilian national team.

item.title: Eleitorado de até 18 anos encolhe 14,5% para as eleições de 2026
item.description: The electorate aged up to 18 years decreased by 14.52% from 2022 to 2026, dropping from 4.18 million to 3.57 million voters, according to TSE data. Despite the decline, women remain the majority in this age group, with 1.83 million female voters versus 1.74 million male voters, mirroring the national trend of female predominance in the Brazilian electorate.

item.title: TCU arquiva processo sobre viagem de Janja aos Estados Unidos
item.description: The Federal Court of Accounts (TCU) dismissed a request for an audit of First Lady Janja da Silva’s official trip to the United States in September 2025, finding no irregularities. The decision relied on opinions from the TCU’s Specialized Audit Unit for Governance and Innovation, which concluded her participation in the delegation complied with the law, supported by Decree 12.604/2025 and AGU’s Normative Orientation 94/2025.

item.title: Ao STF, Valdemar nega indicação de emendas e diz fazer ‘sugestão política’ a parlamentares
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the Liberal Party (PL), told the Supreme Federal Court (STF) he has no authority to indicate parliamentary amendments, stating he only makes non-binding 'political suggestions' to party legislators. His defense argued he never claimed to indicate amendments himself or that other party presidents do so, emphasizing that final decisions rest solely with parliamentarians, their leaders, and thematic committees. Minister Flávio Dino had requested clarifications after an interview in which Valdemar suggested other party presidents indicate amendments.

item.title: Michelle Bolsonaro diz que 'direita do Ceará está vendida' após Ciro afirmar que avalia apoiar Renan ou Caiado ao Planalto
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro criticized the right in Cear�, claiming it was 'sold' for considering support for Ciro Gomes, who said he is evaluating backing Renan Santos or Ronaldo Caiado in the 2026 presidential race. The comment followed public tensions within the Bolsonaro clan between Michelle and Fl�vio Bolsonaro over local political alliances in Cear�.

item.title: Campanha de Lula se divide em dois QGs em Brasília
item.description: President Lula's re-election campaign has split into two locations in Brasília: a mansion in Lago Sul housing the social media team and TV propaganda production, including a recording studio often used by First Lady Janja, and a room in the Commercial South Sector near the PT national headquarters, where the administrative team and government plan developers, including the treasury, are based.

item.title: Advogado de Zambelli prepara candidatura à Câmara pelo Novo
item.description: Lawyer Fábio Pagnozzi, who defends former deputy Carla Zambelli (PL-SP), is preparing to run for a seat in the Chamber of Deputies in 2026 under the Novo party in São Paulo. According to Metrópoles, he is actively building his political project and expects to gain political support. His candidacy is linked to his defense of Zambelli, which may appeal to conservative voters.

item.title: PSDB confirma Ciro Gomes como candidato ao governo do Ceará
item.description: The PSDB-Cidadania federation officially confirmed Ciro Gomes as its gubernatorial candidate for Ceará in a convention held in Fortaleza, with backing from the PL and União Brasil. The full slate remains pending the conventions of allied parties to finalize the vice-governor and senatorial candidates, with Roberto Cláudio, Alcides Fernandes, and Capitão Wagner expected to fill those roles.

item.title: Gleisi diz que família Bolsonaro articulou tarifas dos EUA contra o Brasil
item.description: Gleisi Hoffmann accused the Bolsonaro family of orchestrating U.S. tariffs against Brazil and acting in favor of the U.S. government, posing a risk to national sovereignty. She stated that the Lula government will not negotiate Pix with the U.S., calling it a Brazilian heritage, and criticized Flávio Bolsonaro for supporting such negotiations. She argued that political opponents prioritize foreign interests over the well-being of the Brazilian people.

item.title: Brasil tem 158,7 milhões de eleitores e maioria de mulheres, diz TSE
item.description: Brazil has 158.7 million eligible voters for the 2026 elections, a 1.46% increase from 2022. Women make up 52.84% of the electorate, totaling 83.8 million female voters. The Northern region saw the highest proportional growth at 4.37%, led by Roraima (9.63%) and Tocantins (8.07%), while the Southwest region slightly declined by 0.56%. Voter registration abroad rose 31.82% to 918 million, and the 60+ age group gained the most voters (+4.5 million).

item.title: Tarcísio isenta guardas municipais de ICMS na compra de armas
item.description: The Tarcísio de Freitas government announced an ICMS tax exemption for the purchase of weapons and ammunition by Municipal Civil Guards in 645 São Paulo municipalities. The measure aims to strengthen the operational capacity of local security forces. The decision was announced on July 20, 2026, at 2:41 PM.

item.title: Republicanos escolhe Garotinho para disputar governo do Rio
item.description: The Republicans party has selected Anthony Garotinho as its candidate for governor of Rio de Janeiro in the October elections, following an internal dispute with André Português. The decision, made by the state leadership, will be formalized at a party convention on Saturday, July 25. Garotinho, former governor of Rio (1999-2002) and former mayor of Campos dos Goytacazes, regained his political rights in March after the STF annulled a conviction, making him eligible to run again.

item.title: Os três nomes que Ciro Gomes já disse que poderia apoiar para presidente em 2026
item.description: Ciro Gomes mentioned three names he would support for president in 2026: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), Renan Santos (Missão), and Aldo Rebelo (DC), expressing affinity with Caiado and praise for Santos as a 'novelty' speaking 'very true things'. Despite forming a slate with PL in Ceará, he distances himself from Flávio Bolsonaro and states his final support will depend on a national PSDB agreement led by Aécio Neves.

item.title: Com eleitorado mais velho, Brasil terá 158,7 milhões aptos a votar em 2026, diz TSE
item.description: Brazil will have 158.7 million eligible voters in the 2026 elections, according to the TSE, with a notable aging electorate: 37.5 million are aged 60 or older. This shift may shape campaign priorities, particularly around pensions and healthcare.

item.title: Pix é um sucesso e tarifaço de Trump fortalecerá Lula, diz vencedor do Nobel de Economia
item.description: Nobel laureate economist Paul Krugman praises Pix as a success and rejects U.S. claims of 'unfair competition,' arguing that Trump's proposed tariffs on Brazilian goods will only strengthen Lula by highlighting Brazil's democratic resilience. He contends that Trump's hostility toward Pix stems from protecting his oligarchic donors' interests and fears that such systems could challenge the dollar's global dominance.

item.title: Renan Santos formaliza candidatura à Presidência antes do previsto
item.description: Renan Santos was officially nominated as the Partido Missão's presidential candidate in an online convention on July 20, 2026, moved up due to threats from criminal factions. This marks the first official candidacy registration for the 2026 elections, granting him Federal Police protection, with Aroldo Medina as his running mate. The campaign launch event remains scheduled for August 1 in São Paulo, where the 'Yellow Book' policy document will be unveiled.

item.title: Citando ameaças, Missão antecipa convenção e oficializa Renan Santos como candidato à Presidência
item.description: The Missão Party formally nominated Renan Santos, 42, as its presidential candidate in an advanced convention held on Monday (20), citing threats from criminal factions in Ceará, the PCC in São Paulo, and the CV in Rio de Janeiro as the reason for moving up the event to ensure Federal Police protection.

item.title: Brasil manterá acordos apesar de “postura absurda” dos EUA, diz Padilha
item.description: Health Minister Alexandre Padilha stated that Brazil will maintain international health cooperation agreements, including with U.S. institutions, despite criticizing the U.S. government's posture as 'absurd'. The remarks were made during the signing by President Lula of the legal framework for the Health Economic-Industrial Complex, aimed at strengthening national production of medicines, vaccines, and health technologies to reduce dependence on global supply chains. Padilha cited the incorporation of a bronchiolitis vaccine into the SUS, developed in partnership with an international firm operating in the U.S., as a strategic example of such cooperation.

item.title: Crusoé: Flávio opta pela radicalização
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's pre-campaign has been won by the radical faction, defeating the pragmatic group led by Senator Rogério Marinho. The radicals — comprising the Bolsonaro brothers, overseas bloggers, and hardline bolsonarist legislators — imposed an inflexible ideological line, rejecting moderation in favor of base consolidation.

item.title: Calendário de convenções começa com indefinição dos vices de Flávio Bolsonaro e Romeu Zema
item.description: The party convention season for the 2026 elections began this Monday with several presidential tickets still incomplete. While Lula, Caiado, and Renan Santos have already confirmed their running mates, Flávio Bolsonaro and Romeu Zema continue negotiations to finalize their vice-presidential picks, with the PL senator pushing for a woman on the ticket and seeking PP support, which remains uncertain due to the União Progressista federation's likely neutrality.

item.title: Em largada ao governo do Rio, Paes elogia Couto e chama rivais de ‘organização criminosa’
item.description: Former Rio mayor Eduardo Paes officially launched his gubernatorial campaign under the PSD, with lawyer Jane Reis as his running mate, positioning himself as the frontrunner in polls. In his speech, he praised interim governor Ricardo Couto for his moralizing and spending-cut policies, pledging to continue and deepen them, while advocating a hardline stance against organized crime, including potential federal and military support. He also noted Lula’s backing despite his vice’s Bolsonarist alignment, calling for unity beyond political divides.

item.title: Eleitores podem pedir voto em trânsito a partir de hoje: veja como usar o serviço
item.description: Voters who will be outside their electoral domicile during the 2026 elections can now request absentee voting (voto em trânsito) starting today, July 20, until August 20, via the TSE’s online portal or in person at electoral courts. The service allows temporary reassignment of voting location for the first round (October 4), potential second round (October 25), or both, with the option to select different municipalities per round. Eligibility requires an active electoral registration, and changes can be modified or canceled until the deadline.

item.title: Aliados de Flávio veem gesto de Ciro a Caiado e Renan como afronta, mas evitam confronto para preservar aliança no Ceará
item.description: Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro view Ciro Gomes' statement suggesting possible support for Ronaldo Caiado or Renan Santos as a breach of an informal neutrality pact in the presidential race, but avoid confrontation to preserve their alliance in Ceará. They assess that Ciro remains the most competitive candidate to challenge the PT in the state, and the state-level agreement will be upheld despite behind-the-scenes discomfort. The PL campaign believes Ciro can weaken Lula and Elmano de Freitas, and plans to supply him with anti-federal government material.

item.title: Valdemar nega ter cota de emendas, e diz só sugerir destino do dinheiro
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the Liberal Party, denied having a quota or authority over the allocation of parliamentary amendments, stating he only makes political suggestions after consultations with various societal actors. The statement was made in a submission to the Federal Supreme Court on Monday, July 20, 2026. The report will be updated with additional information.

item.title: Número de eleitores com menos de 18 anos cai 14,5% em 2026
item.description: The Brazilian electorate for the 2026 elections totals 158.7 million eligible voters, with a 13.9% increase in the 60+ age group (from 32.8 to 37.4 million) and a 14.5% decrease among those 18 or younger (from 4.1 to 3.5 million). Women make up 53% of the electorate, men 47%. Voting is optional for ages 16–18 and mandatory from 18 onward.

item.title: PSD oficializa candidatura de Eduardo Paes ao governo do Rio
item.description: The PSD officially nominated Eduardo Paes as its candidate for governor of Rio de Janeiro, with lawyer Jane Reis (MDB) as his running mate for vice-governor. Paes, a four-time mayor of Rio and current poll leader, has the support of President Lula and is making his third bid for state office. The ticket also includes federal deputies Pedro Paulo (PSD) and Benedita da Silva (PT) as Senate candidates.

item.title: O que provocou a mudança de estratégia na campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL-RJ) campaign is shifting strategy amid multiple crises, including family disputes with Michelle Bolsonaro, the 'tariff shock,' poor polling, and the Centrão bloc (União Brasil, PP, Republicanos) opting for neutrality in party conventions. To respond, the team plans to intensify supermarket and market recordings, comparing current food prices with those from 2019—the first year of Jair Bolsonaro's government—to tap into voter dissatisfaction over the cost of living.

item.title: Eleições 2026: veja no mapa o perfil dos eleitores de cada estado
item.description: The TSE released the profile of the Brazilian electorate for the 2026 elections, with 158.8 million eligible voters. São Paulo leads with 34.1 million (21.5% of the total), followed by Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, and Bahia. The 40–44 age group is the largest in 17 states, and high school completion is the predominant education level in 22 federative units.

item.title: TSE: mais de 300 mil pessoas cegas devem votar nas eleições de 2026
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) reported that 319,489 visually impaired voters are expected to participate in the 2026 general elections, representing 0.20% of the national electorate. São Paulo has the highest absolute number with 53,192 blind voters, while Tocantins has the highest proportion at 0.33%. Electronic voting machines with tactile writing and reading systems enable their participation, highlighting Brazil’s progress in electoral accessibility since 1996.

item.title: Saiba onde o eleitorado apto a votar em 2026 mais cresceu no Brasil
item.description: The Brazilian electorate for the 2026 elections reached 158.7 million, an increase of 2.3 million since 2022. The North region led in proportional growth (+4.37%), followed by the Central-West (+3.97%), while the Northeast had the largest absolute increase (+1.1 million). The Southeast was the only region to decline (-0.56%), reducing its national share.

item.title: Novo Bolsa Família e celular grátis: o que vem no plano Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro proposes transforming Bolsa Família into a broader income transfer platform that includes professional training and credit access, maintaining benefits for up to two years for beneficiaries who secure formal employment or open a MEI, with potential cashbacks for courses and cheap microcredit from Caixa. The plan also promises free internet for 70 million women and cellphone distribution for low-income groups, contrasting with market demands for fiscal austerity, as his economic team projects R$ 217 billion in spending cuts by 2027 without specifying funding sources.

item.title: Republicanos anuncia Anthony Garotinho como candidato a governador do Rio
item.description: The Republicans party has nominated Anthony Garotinho as its candidate for governor of Rio de Janeiro in 2026, following an internal contest against André Português. Garotinho, a former three-time governor, regained eligibility after the Supreme Federal Court annulled an electoral conviction. The party has also nominated Marcelo Crivella for the Senate.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula sanciona projeto para fortalecer indústria da saúde
item.description: President Lula signed into law Bill 2.583/2020, establishing the National Strategy for the Healthcare Economic-Industrial Complex to strengthen domestic production of medicines, supplies, and health technologies. The ceremony took place at 11 a.m. at the Planalto Palace, attended by Health Minister Alexandre Padilha. The initiative aims to reduce import dependence and boost innovation and technological sovereignty in Brazil’s health sector.

item.title: Valdemar: Falta gesto de Flávio Bolsonaro para encerrar briga com Michelle
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto, president of the PL, stated that a gesture from Flávio Bolsonaro is lacking to end the feud with Michelle Bolsonaro, commenting on the internal dispute within the Bolsonarist camp. The remark was made in an interview with UOL News, emphasizing the need for reconciliation among Bolsonaro family members to strengthen the political group.

item.title: Lula brinca e diz que tarifaço é com “Stuckinha”
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) joked about the US tariff on Brazilian goods, saying the matter was with 'Stuckinha', the nickname of his official photographer Ricardo Stuckert, while leaving the Planalto Palace for the signing of the National Strategy for the Health Economic-Industrial Complex. The 25% US tariff on Brazilian products takes effect on July 22, and the government expects negotiations with the US to advance only after the October elections, awaiting clarity on Brazil’s political landscape.

item.title: Toffoli manda à PGR queixa-crime de Flávio contra Janones por ser chamado de ‘miliciano’
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Dias Toffoli has ordered the Attorney General's Office (PGR) to rule on a criminal complaint filed by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro against federal deputy André Janones for alleged slander, after Janones referred to him as a 'miliciano' and other insults in social media videos between March and June 2026. Bolsonaro seeks at least R$200,000 in moral damages, arguing the statements went beyond political criticism and constituted gratuitous offense. His defense claims parliamentary immunity does not apply because the remarks were made online.

item.title: TCU arquiva processo sobre viagens de Janja
item.description: The TCU archived the investigation into alleged irregularities in the international trips of First Lady Janja, concluding that expenses were regular and there was no misuse of public funds. The decision followed AGU guidance and decrees recognizing the public interest nature of the presidential spouse's role, despite her not holding public office. The specific archiving of the New York trip in September 2025 came after a broader review in process TC 000.031/2025-9, which had already dismissed the accusations as unfounded.

item.title: Vai decolar o 'Aerosalomão', caravana de juízes para a posse de Luis Felipe Salomão no comando do STJ
item.description: A group of judges and appellate judges from Rio de Janeiro, nicknamed 'Aerosalomão', will travel to Brasília on August 19 for the inauguration of Luis Felipe Salomão as the new president of the Superior Court of Justice (STJ) for the 2026-2028 term. Salomão, aged 63, assumes the post following his nomination and Senate approval. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Toffoli manda à PGR queixa-crime de Flávio contra Janones por xingamentos: ‘Miliciano’ e ‘bandido’
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Dias Toffoli has forwarded a criminal complaint filed by presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) against Congressman André Janones for defamation, after Janones called him a 'miliciano' and 'bandido' in videos from March to June. Flávio is also seeking R$20,000 in moral damages. Janones faces a similar lawsuit from Michelle Bolsonaro, who alleges he falsely accused her of receiving 'stolen money' from banker Daniel Vorcaro.

item.title: Kim atuará como advogado de Renan nas eleições
item.description: Federal deputy Kim Kataguiri announced he will serve as lawyer for Renan Santos' presidential candidacy in the 2026 elections, following the virtual convention of the Missão party. Renan Santos will run for president with Aroldo Medina as his running mate, according to Kim. The ticket was officially confirmed by the Missão party.

item.title: Eleitorado no exterior registra alta de 31,82% para as Eleições 2026
item.description: The Brazilian electorate abroad increased by 31.82% for the 2026 elections, rising from 697,078 to 918,876 voters, according to TSE data. This represents 0.58% of the total electorate, up from 0.45% in 2022, with 221,863 new voters added. These overseas voters can only participate in the presidential election, while other offices will be decided by voters residing in Brazil.

item.title: PF inicia a segurança de candidatos à Presidência; Flávio Bolsonaro recusa proteção
item.description: The Federal Police launched a national security operation for presidential candidates in the 2026 elections, designed to protect up to ten candidacies with risk-based planning, surveillance technology, and coordination with state and local forces. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) declined the protection, citing distrust in the PF leadership and fears of agent infiltration within his team. The PF confirmed participation is voluntary and that candidates’ decisions will be honored.

item.title: O mais novo entrevero entre aliados de Flávio e Valdemar
item.description: Ideological allies within the PL party expressed discomfort after Valdemar Costa Neto’s interview with Globo, in which he questioned Daniella Marques’ electoral viability as a running mate for Flávio Bolsonaro. He stated she lacks the conditions to join the 2026 presidential ticket.

item.title: Nobel de Economia elogia o Pix e diz que tarifaço “fortalecerá” Lula
item.description: Nobel laureate economist Paul Krugman praised Brazil's Pix instant payment system and argued that the 25% U.S. tariff on Brazilian imports will politically strengthen President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Writing in The New York Times, he suggested the external pressure could foster national unity around Lula's government.

item.title: Número de eleitores cresce e Brasil tem 158,7 milhões aptos a votar
item.description: The number of eligible voters in Brazil has reached 158,745,463, an increase of 2.3 million compared to the 2022 elections, when there were 156,454,011. TSE data shows that 89.01% of the electorate now has biometric registration. The 2026 elections will decide presidential, gubernatorial, federal legislative, and state/district offices.

item.title: Não lembra? Recorda quem ainda está vivo na Sul-Americana, Libertadores, Copa do Brasil e quem disputa o título no Brasileirão
item.description: Following the 2026 World Cup break, Brazilian and South American football enters the decisive stage: the Libertadores has its round of 16 set, featuring matches like Palmeiras vs Cerro Porteño and the sole Brazilian clash Flamengo vs Cruzeiro; the Sudamericana grants direct qualification to Atlético-MG, Botafogo, and São Paulo, while Grêmio, Vasco, Bragantino, and Santos must go through playoffs; the Copa do Brasil reaches the round of 16 with key ties Fluminense vs Vasco and Corinthians vs Internacional; the Brasileirão resumes with Palmeiras leading at 41 points, Flamengo second with 34 (one game in hand), Fluminense third with 32, and Bragantino fourth with 30.

item.title: Marco Rubio usa candidatura de Flávio Bolsonaro para se tornar vice-rei do Brasil
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) is portrayed as a candidate backed by Marco Rubio, U.S. Secretary of State, to run for Brazil’s presidency in 2026, aiming to serve U.S. interests through tariff pressure. The text claims that the 25% U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods are intended to force openness in high-value sectors and position Bolsonaro as a White House proxy in the Planalto Palace. It criticizes Lula for allegedly prioritizing ego over national interests by refusing to yield to U.S. demands, while arguing that Brazilian sovereignty requires resistance to such external pressure.

item.title: Comissão presidida pelo PT passa o ano sem fiscalizar o governo
item.description: The Financial Oversight and Control Commission (CFFC) of the Chamber of Deputies, chaired by Deputy Alexandre Lindenmeyer (PT-RS), ended 2026 without approving any request for audit, oversight, or summons of federal authorities. The committee, responsible for monitoring public policy execution and the use of federal funds, failed to exercise its oversight function throughout the year.

item.title: A nova baixa na chapa do PL no Rio
item.description: Rogério Lisboa withdrew from the PL's vice-governor ticket in Rio after pressure from Eduardo Paes (PSD), who had already allied with the MDB and nominated Jane Reis as his running mate. This marks the third defection from the Bolsonaro-aligned slate in Rio, following the withdrawals of Cláudio Castro and Márcio Canella from the Senate race due to PF investigations. The PL is racing to finalize its ticket before its Saturday convention to meet the candidate registration deadline.
